show: Latent Space: The AI Engineer Podcast
titel: 🔬 “We have foundation models for language, not for physics” — Anima Anandkumar, Bren Professor of Computing

faehigkeiten.grund: Dynamik weder belegt noch ausgeschlossen: keine Merkmale gefunden, aber eine unveraenderte Wiederholungsprobe beweist nichts

einzeiler: Anima Anandkumar on neural operators, physics-informed AI, and climate modeling.
kurzfassung: Anima Anandkumar discusses how neural operators bridge artificial intelligence and the physical world. She explains their applications in weather forecasting, fusion energy, and scientific discovery. The conversation also covers the importance of mathematical verification and domain-specific AI architectures.
stichpunkte: Neural operators model continuous function spaces, enabling zero-shot super-resolution.
Traditional physics-informed neural networks struggle with turbulent or chaotic time-dependent problems.
FourCastNet demonstrates that AI weather models can be tens of thousands of times faster than traditional solvers.
Incorporating spherical geometry allows AI models to perform stable, long-term climate simulations.
TorchLean integrates neural networks with formal proof assistants to provide certified robustness guarantees.
Digital twins of tokamaks help model complex plasma behavior and develop control mechanisms for fusion reactors.
Scientific AI requires high resolution and domain-specific architectural inductive biases rather than standard transformer approaches.

kapitel.titel: AI for Science and Future Outlook

clips.hook: Tens of thousands of times faster than traditional weather models
clips.text: Neural operators capture weather phenomena with high accuracy while running drastically faster than conventional methods.

clips.hook: Modeling inputs and outputs as continuous functions
clips.text: Neural operators handle infinite resolution by treating data as continuous functions rather than fixed grids.

clips.hook: Hundreds of billions to a trillion context length
clips.text: High-resolution physical simulations demand context lengths that completely exceed the capacity of standard transformer architectures.

clips.hook: Assuming the world is a rectangle versus a sphere
clips.text: Standard architectures quickly blow up during long rollouts because they fail to account for the actual geometry of the Earth.

clips.hook: AI for science is different from language models
clips.text: Regulatory frameworks often treat all artificial intelligence the same, overlooking the unique discovery potential of scientific AI.
